summary: All four gates green, all three defects independently reproduced as fixed and each mutation-confirmed Red, contract byte-identical to attempt 1, no new defects, concurrency tests stable over 5 runs.
gates: lint=0 type-check=0 test=0 integration=0 api=24/248 integration=16/73 (web 28/181, shared-utils 1/17; baselines api 23/215 and integration 13/47, nothing removed)
acceptance_proven: yes - all seven clauses proven, each by a test whose inversion I watched go Red; see report section 9
defect1_fixed: yes - 90 genuinely concurrent same-name createFuncao calls in ONE org: 0 unhandled, 1 winner, 89 sentinels (previous pass measured 60/90 raising 23505). Both 409 reasons independently reachable: 'duplicate' on same name and 'duplicate_slug' on a distinct display name with the same derived slug, sequentially, and under concurrency the 90-way rename probe produced 66 duplicate + 21 duplicate_slug. Mutation M1 (plain INSERT) -> Red, 36/48 unhandled 23505; mutation M2 (drop the SAVEPOINT + violation mapping from updateFuncao) -> Red, 18 unhandled. Each mutation reddens only its own test.
defect2_fixed: yes - characterisation reproduced and confirmed against the mutant: 30 orgs x 5 hit on 6 of 6 runs (4-9 unhandled each, always 23505 on sales_ops_funcoes_org_name_idx), while 4 orgs x 24 hit on only 3 of 6 (0,0,0,1,2,0), so the per-fresh-org claim is directionally right though the literal '0 of 96' is optimistic. On the current code both shapes ran 6 consecutive times each, 1476 calls total, 0 unhandled and 0 spurious sentinels.
defect3_fixed: yes - verified the client myself (SalesOpsApp.tsx:3425 builds contactEmail.trim() || undefined, api.ts:72 JSON.stringify drops it) and printed the real serialized body, which has no contactEmail key at all. That exact body through UpdatePersonSchema into updatePerson clears both the returned row and the stored contact_email column, and leaves the funcao set intact. Present-and-empty also clears; a real address still round-trips. Mutation M4 (conditional spread) -> Red.
two_test_approach_judged: legitimate - BOTH tests catch the narrow-arbiter mutation on all 5 consecutive runs, so the deterministic guard is not carrying the load alone; the 30-org race test is itself a deterministic reproducer (and my own probe reproduced 6/6). The deterministic guard is a valid second oracle because it exercises exactly the arbiter-visibility property the fix changes with zero timing dependence, and it cannot pass while the real defect returns since the real defect IS the narrow arbiter. Its fixture state is genuinely API-unreachable (slug always tracks name), which is why it needs the admin client, and the test documents that.
new_defects_from_fixes: none - the bare onConflictDoNothing can only fire on the two org-scoped unique indexes (a same-name row in another org provably cannot conflict, verified), never returns success when nothing was written, and does not loop; the re-probe falls back to a 409 rather than a false success when the winner is uncommitted. The SAVEPOINT was verified against the driver source (drizzle 0.45.2 delegates to postgres.js sql.savepoint, which issues rollback-to-savepoint on ANY throw and rethrows), exactly one savepoint per short transaction so nothing accumulates, and empirically 0 backends left idle-in-transaction over 20 rounds of forced contention. Constraint-name coupling is brittle but GUARDED: renaming the keys (M2b) reddens the integration gate, so a renamed index cannot silently turn a 409 back into a 500. Restoring the unconditional contactEmail is byte-for-byte the pre-slice semantic and cannot regress anything relative to master; it does not disturb the funcoes set-replace.
concurrency_tests_flaky: no - 5 consecutive full integration runs (4 back-to-back plus one earlier), 16 files / 73 tests passing and exit 0 every single time; counts perfectly stable
previous_properties_still_hold: yes - tenancy: deleting listFuncoes' orgId filter Red, deleting resolvePersonFuncoes' security-critical ids-branch filter Red, and the one surviving filter (attachPersonFuncoes) is a provably equivalent mutant given the composite FK plus caller-side scoping. Mirrors: 3 of 4 drift mutations Red. Migration: db:generate reports no schema changes with a clean git status, and a from-scratch 13-migration replay onto a throwaway DB produced a byte-identical normalized catalog (sha 28875d07 both sides). is_system: CHECK constraint present and rejecting raw superuser SQL on both INSERT and UPDATE, plus both service guards mutation-Red. Composite FK downgrade Red. Backfill: all 8 migration tests green including seller+finder as ONE pessoa with BOTH funcoes, and idempotent across three replays.
